research_result.description: Cloudflare is a cloud platform offering security, performance, serverless compute, and infrastructure services with extensive REST and GraphQL APIs and native Model Context Protocol (MCP) support.
research_result.credential_requirements: Developers can sign up for a free Cloudflare account using an email address and password to generate API tokens or retrieve API keys. While initial setup and basic usage are free, usage-based billing or paid plan subscriptions apply for elevated infrastructure usage.

evidence.claim: Cloudflare supports authentication using API tokens.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Create an API token to grant access to the API to perform actions.
As an industry-standard protocol for authorization, OAuth 2.0 enables applications to obtain limited access to user accounts on an HTTP service.

evidence.claim: Cloudflare supports authentication using Global API keys as a legacy mechanism.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Global API key is the previous authorization scheme for interacting with the Cloudflare API.

evidence.claim: Cloudflare accounts can be created via self-serve sign up.

evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Use the following resources to learn more about Cloudflare's REST API:
Interact with Cloudflare services programmatically using the REST and GraphQL APIs.

evidence.claim: Cloudflare natively supports building and deploying Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: You can build and deploy Model Context Protocol (MCP) ↗ servers on Cloudflare.
